- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is rising.
- Overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment (≥0.67) precede forecast, model often overreacts; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to prevent overcorrection.
- If true outcome is consistently below forecast for 5+ days, model may be ignoring mean reversion; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% per day until trend stabilizes.
- For 30-day horizon, if sentiment is neutral or mixed, model often overfits recent volatility; use 3–5 day moving average to smooth forecast.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model often fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If forecast is consistently 1–2% above true outcome for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward correction of 0.5–1.0% per day to avoid overconfidence bias.
